references.text: Describes the LORD as a consuming fire, the same expression as in Exodus 24:17 (אֵ֥שׁ אֹכְלָ֖ה)
The LORD is described as a consuming fire going before Israel, parallel to the revelation at Sinai
Describes the fire on Mount Sinai when the LORD came down, same context as Exodus 24:17
The angel of the LORD appears in a flame of fire, an early manifestation of God's glory through fire
Ezekiel's vision of the glory of God (כְּב֣וֹד יְהוָ֔ה) with a fire-like appearance, parallel to the Sinai revelation
The prophecy that the LORD will create fire and flame over Mount Zion, echoing the glory of Sinai
Question about who can dwell with consuming fire, referring to God's holy presence
Refers to the Sinai experience with fire that burned, contrasting with the new covenant
Quotes that our God is a consuming fire (πῦρ καταναλίσκον), direct parallel to Exodus 24:17
Ezekiel recognizes the glory from Sinai (Ex 24) as a constant reference for God's presence, even when threatened by idolatry.
The verses together form a complete description of God's revelation at Sinai: the clear heavenly nature (v.10) manifested as a dangerous, consuming fire (v.17).
The dedication of the temple repeats and confirms the Sinai event: the Lord's glory appearing as fire visible to all people marks God's new dwelling.
Ezekiel's vision of God's glory lighting up the earth mirrors the visible manifestation at Sinai, emphasizing that God is the same in judgment and restoration.
The 'consuming fire' on Sinai (Ex 24) becomes the guiding fire over the tabernacle (Ex 40), showing God's continuous presence from revelation to journey.
